intel.t: Get Nevada "out of this Lombardo Trump economy": lower costs, limits on corporate home buying, a drug price cap, data centers that pay for their own power, and a governor who is not bought by billionaire donors.

intel.l: Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it
intel.t: "High Flyin' Ford": corporate funded attorney general trips and the claim he missed 420 days of work, backed by an ethics complaint a panel advanced in February; Ford says every trip was disclosed and he has no regrets.
Hispanic voters, 51 to 20, and women, 48 to 37, in Emerson's September poll, plus organized labor led by the Culinary Union's door knocking.

Public safety and crime, where voters trust Lombardo by 12 points, with independents tied at 32 and no party candidate Danielle Ford at 7 percent in Noble Predictive Insights; his favorable rating of 41 to 38 trails Lombardo's 49 to 39 in Emerson.
Kamala Harris rallied for him at the Culinary Union in Las Vegas on October 22, 2026, calling him a chance to elect Nevada's first Black governor.

He trails: $1.3 million campaign cash to Lombardo's $2.8 million, nearly $2.7 million in PAC money to more than $5.8 million excluding governors groups, and $14.1 million in DGA side ads to $29.3 million for Better Nevada PAC, though his campaign outraised Lombardo's directly in the third quarter.

bottom: Ford won the June 9 primary with 63.3 percent over Alexis Hill, per Ballotpedia, https://ballotpedia.org/Aaron_Ford_%28Nevada%29. In 2026 through September 30 his campaign raised almost $5 million and Forward Nevada PAC just over $4 million, per KTVN on October 20, 2026, https://www.2news.com/townnews/economics/looking-at-recent-2026-nevada-campaign-finance-reports/article_d3235f09-5701-4e00-a585-e50de6ffc1bb.html. In the third quarter he raised more in direct gifts than Lombardo for the first time, almost $2.3 million to just over $1.5 million, but entered October with $1.3 million in cash to Lombardo's $2.8 million, per The Nevada Independent on October 17, 2026, https://thenevadaindependent.com/article/our-top-takeaways-from-nevadas-new-campaign-finance-reports.
Three interests combine money and a decision:

**Labor unions.** AFSCME gave Forward Nevada PAC $500,000 in each of the second and third quarters. SEIU gave $250,000 and the IBEW PAC Educational Fund $200,000. The Culinary Union is canvassing for him. The lever is right to work repeal, the budget and labor bills Lombardo vetoed.
**The Democratic Governors Association.** $7 million to A More Affordable Nevada PAC in the third quarter, which had spent or reserved more than $14.1 million in ads.

intel.t: A record of results and restraint: education, health care, public safety and the economy, a no new taxes pledge and a record veto pen against the Democratic Legislature, paired with attacks on Ford's out of state travel.

intel.l: Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it
intel.t: The "Lombardo Trump economy": high fuel, housing and health costs, his tariff remark that people should "feel a little pain," vetoes of drug cost and renter bills, and policies Ford says serve billionaire donors like Bigelow.

White voters, 51 to 38, and men, 47 to 41, in Emerson's September poll, with a 49 to 39 favorable rating; voters trust him over Ford on public safety and crime by 12 points in Noble Predictive Insights.
Hispanic voters, where he trails 20 to 51, and Trump's 37 to 55 approval among likely voters; his economic approval is 45 to 47 in Noble, and RedBox Research had him down 43 to 46 on October 23.

At an October fundraiser he said "There's no place easier to vote in the nation than Nevada. Unfortunately," reported by the Nevada Current on October 22 and pushed by the state Democratic Party; his campaign did not comment. Earlier he skipped the October 9 Carson City forum, leaving Ford at an empty podium.

He leads: $2.8 million campaign cash to Ford's $1.3 million, more than $5.8 million in PAC money to Ford's $2.7 million excluding governors groups, and $29.3 million in Better Nevada PAC ads to $14.1 million for the DGA side, though Ford outraised his campaign directly in the third quarter.

bottom: Lombardo runs a three vehicle operation: his campaign committee, Better Nevada PAC and Nevada Way PAC. Direct gifts to the campaign are capped at $10,000, so the big money sits in the PACs. In 2026 through September 30 his campaign raised just over $6 million and Better Nevada PAC about $30 million, per KTVN on October 20, 2026, https://www.2news.com/townnews/economics/looking-at-recent-2026-nevada-campaign-finance-reports/article_d3235f09-5701-4e00-a585-e50de6ffc1bb.html. He entered October with $2.8 million in campaign cash to Ford's $1.3 million, per The Nevada Independent on October 17, 2026, https://thenevadaindependent.com/article/our-top-takeaways-from-nevadas-new-campaign-finance-reports. Better Nevada PAC had spent or reserved more than $29.3 million in ads, about twice the DGA side.
Five interests combine large money and a live decision:

**Billionaire megadonors.** Robert Bigelow, the Budget Suites weekly motel owner, gave Better Nevada PAC $2.5 million in the second quarter and gave $6 million to the RGA's Nevada PAC in the third. Ben Horowitz and his wife gave $1 million. The lever is housing and landlord law, where Lombardo has used his veto.
**The Republican Governors Association.** $5 million to Better Nevada PAC in the second quarter and $9.5 million to a Lombardo affiliated PAC in the third.

D.t: Aaron Ford leads by 5.1 in the forecast and wins 81% of simulations. The cushion is about 62,751 votes; a one point swing is about 6,164 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +2.4 and D +12.6. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is D +1.3. Your best recent poll is Hart Research (D) at D +3.0; your worst is Global Strategy Group for Ford (D) at R +3.5. 4 polls in the last 30 days.
The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Clark, a projected net 112,522 votes; Washoe, a projected net 11,890 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Washoe, D +5.4, 18.0% of the vote; Carson City, R +8.3, 2.2% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Aaron Ford runs furthest behind in Douglas, Lyon, Elko. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Large counties, 87% of voters, 53 to 43, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.34 points; White voters, 67% of voters, 41 to 54, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.33 points; Voters without a degree, 66% of voters, 50 to 46, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.33 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Aaron Ford: Immigration voters 23 to 73, Small counties 27 to 67, Voters who can afford daily costs 41 to 55. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
